info.inflation: How much consumer prices changed compared with the same month a year earlier. 5% means that what cost 100 GEL a year ago now costs about 105 GEL. Below zero, prices fell.
info.measures: Headline inflation covers everything in the consumer basket. Core inflation leaves out the most volatile prices, such as food and energy, so it shows the underlying trend. The harmonised index (HICP) follows the EU method and can be compared with European countries.
info.components: Inflation split into four parts of the basket: food, alcohol and tobacco; energy (fuel, electricity, gas); other goods; services. The line furthest from zero pushes overall inflation the most.
info.groups: Annual price change in each consumption group for the selected city in the latest month. Bars to the left of zero (red) mean prices in that group fell.
info.groupTrend: Annual inflation of the chosen consumption group compared with total inflation in the selected city. When the group's line is above the total, it pushes inflation up.
info.cities: Annual inflation in the six cities where Geostat collects prices, and in Georgia as a whole, in the latest month.
info.basket: How much each group weighs when Geostat calculates inflation, based on what households spend. Food is about a third of the basket, so a rise in food prices moves the CPI about three times as much as the same rise in transport.
info.producer: Prices that producers receive and prices of exports and imports, compared with their 2020 average (= 100). 150 means 50% higher than in 2020. Producer prices often change before shop prices.
info.construction: Cost of building inputs compared with February 2022 (= 100): materials, construction workers' wages, machinery, and transport and energy.
info.tbilisi: Median price of one square metre of housing in each Tbilisi district in the latest quarter. Median: half of the properties are cheaper and half more expensive. Darker districts are more expensive.
info.rppi: Residential property price index for the whole country compared with the 2020 average (= 100), for flats, houses and all dwellings.
info.product: Average shop price across Georgia, in GEL per the unit shown in the list (for example 1 kg). Switch to the index to compare products with very different prices: every product starts at 100 in January 2020, so 150 means 50% more expensive than then.
info.movers: Products whose average price changed the most over the last 12 months.
info.salary: Nominal is the average monthly salary in GEL as actually paid. Real removes the effect of inflation: it shows what that salary is worth at 2010 prices (nominal salary divided by the consumer price index). If the real line rises, salaries grow faster than prices and people can buy more. If the nominal line rises but the real line is flat, the raise was eaten by inflation.
info.realGrowth: Change in the real (inflation-adjusted) salary compared with the same quarter a year earlier. Red bars: salaries grew more slowly than prices, so purchasing power fell.
info.activity: Average monthly salary in each economic activity in the latest quarter, for the selected sex or sector.
info.sex: Average salaries of women and men. The gap shows how much less women earn on average; it partly reflects different jobs and working hours, not only different pay for the same work.
info.wageRegion: Average monthly salary of employees by region in the latest quarter. 'Total' is the country average.
info.unemp: Share of the labour force — people who work or are actively looking for work — that has no job. Students, retirees and people who have stopped looking are not in the labour force.
info.rates: Participation rate: share of people aged 15+ who work or look for work. Employment rate: share of people aged 15+ who work.
info.labourRegion: Annual Labour Force Survey results by region for the selected year and indicator. 'Georgia' is the country figure.
info.growth: How much the economy's output grew after removing price changes, compared with the same period a year earlier. Lighter bars are preliminary estimates that Geostat may revise.
info.perCapita: Gross domestic product divided by the population, converted to US dollars at the average exchange rate. A stronger or weaker lari also moves this figure.
info.fx: Average number of lari for one US dollar in each quarter. A falling line means the lari got stronger.
info.sectors: Share of each economic activity in the economy's total value added in the latest year.
info.sectorGrowth: Real growth of the selected sector compared with the same period a year earlier, with price changes removed.
info.fdi: Money invested in Georgian businesses by foreign companies and individuals, by year, in million US dollars.
info.flows: Exports and imports of goods and services from the national accounts. When imports are above exports, Georgia buys more from abroad than it sells.
info.balance: Exports minus imports. Red bars below zero: a trade deficit in that period.
info.composition: Exports split into goods and services. Services exports are mostly tourism and transport.
info.open: Exports and imports as a share of GDP show how open the economy is to trade.
info.population: Number of people living in Georgia on 1 January, not counting the occupied territories.
info.populationRegions: Population of each region on 1 January of the selected year.
info.pyramid: Men on the left, women on the right, by 5-year age group. A wide base means many children; a narrow base means fewer births in recent years.
info.poverty: Share of people whose spending is below the absolute poverty line: the cost of a minimum food basket plus basic non-food needs.
info.map: Darker areas have higher values. Grey areas have no data (occupied territories). Business statistics cover enterprises registered in each area; the latest year is 2022.
info.areaTrend: How the selected indicator changed over the years in the selected area.
